gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2, ChatGPT's 'best all-around' car-camping pick, lists no car-charging input on Anker's US spec sheet and ships with only an AC cable, will not charge below 32°F, and only fast-charges once its cells are above 68°F, so recharging at camp depends on its 600 W solar port.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited. GearJunkie (gearjunkie.com/technology/best-portable-power-stations) has part of it. It gives a general rule that units are 'never used (charged or discharged) below 32 degrees F, though that varies a bit by model and brand'. It gives no car-socket charging wattage, nothing on what comes in the box, and nothing on the 68°F fast-charge threshold. OutdoorGearLab (best-power-station) gives no charging temperature range at all. Its only car-charging figure is the EcoFlow Delta Pro's 800 W, and it calls a 12 V car cable 'a low-cost way to recharge' without saying which units can use one. I could not open the uncited top results (Tested Watts, WIRED, Outdoor Life) within the call budget.
decides: For a car camper who wants to top up from the vehicle or charge on cold mornings, this cuts into the C1000 Gen 2 pick. Its 1,600 W wall charging is useless at a campsite. Anker's US page lists no car input and no car cable in the box. Below 32°F it won't take a charge at all, and between 32°F and 68°F charging is 'significantly' slower. If the shopper won't have mains power or a solar panel, the answer should point them to a unit with a stated car-charging input and an included cable, or to the Anker alternator charger. On a cold trip, the battery should go in the car to warm up before charging. The pick stands if they'll charge from mains or solar in mild weather.

findings.label: Charging temperature range
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (Anker SOLIX US product page)
findings.note: Spec sheet line 'Charging Temperature 32°F - 104°F'. Discharging is listed separately as -4°F to 104°F, so the unit can power devices below freezing but cannot recharge.

findings.label: UltraFast charging cell-temperature threshold
findings.value: Activates only above 68°F (20°C) cell temperature; charging at 32–68°F 'will significantly reduce charging speed'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (Anker SOLIX US product page)
findings.note: Anker's wording: 'UltraFast Charging activates when the battery temperature is above 20 °C (68 °F).' The threshold is cell temperature, not air temperature.

findings.label: Car charging input / car cable in box
findings.value: No car-charging input listed. In the box: power station, AC charging cable, user manual and safety card only.
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (Anker SOLIX US product page)
findings.note: The only car-socket item on the spec sheet is an output: 'Car Charger 12V⎓10A, 120W'. Box contents quoted from the page.

findings.label: Solar (MPPT) input
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (Anker SOLIX US product page)
findings.note: This is my inference, not Anker's statement: if a car-socket-to-XT60 cable works on this port, a 12 V socket is capped at about 12 V × 8.2 A ≈ 98 W, so 1,024 Wh / 98 W ≈ 10.4 h for a full charge before conversion losses. Anker does not state car charging for this model.
